## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 69, titled *Ukkhittasambhoga* ("Living with an ejected monk"), establishes an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) for any monk who knowingly associates with, eats with (*sambhuñjeyya*), lives with (*saṁvāseyya*), or shares a sleeping place (*saha vā seyyaṁ kappeyya*) with a monk who holds the pernicious view that things declared by the Buddha to be obstructive are not obstructive (referring back to Pācittiya 68) and who has been suspended without having renounced that view [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. 

In the wording of the rule, such an individual is described as *akatānudhammena* ("not dealt with according to Dhamma"), which the Vibhaṅga's word commentary explains as suspended and not rehabilitated (*ukkhitto anosārito*) [Dutt, Early Buddhist Monachism; Hüsken 1997]. Sukumar Dutt notes that this phrase presupposes the formal disciplinary act of suspension (*ukkhepaniyakamma*), a procedure codified in the Khandhakas (such as Cullavagga I) [Dutt, Early Buddhist Monachism]. Commentators and Vinaya studies observe that this rule acts as a disciplinary and preventive measure against communal schism (*saṅghabheda*), ensuring that monks do not maintain regular communion or establish separate factions with an unrepentant suspended monastic [Hahn et al. 1997; Hüsken 1997].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this rule was preserved across nearly all early Buddhist monastic lineages, including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya Vinayas, as well as in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Pācittiya 147) and Parivāra [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identifies extensive textual reuse within the Pali canon, notably sharing long passages with Pācittiya 70, Pācittiya 68, the Kammakkhandhaka (Kd 11), and the *Alagaddūpama Sutta* (MN 22), along with cross-language alignments to the Sanskrit *Pāṇḍulohitakavastu* and *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* [DharmaNexus]. An English translation has been provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
